hero.storyTitle: Good years. Difficult years. A better balance.
hero.storyBody: Viora brings winter chill, fruit load and thinning guidance together, helping olive growers plan the next harvest, tree by tree.

intro.description: We combine field sensors, weather forecasts and tree-by-tree sampling to turn alternate bearing into decisions. From the first chill alert to the end of the season, Viora tells you what to do and how much to expect from your harvest.
intro.aboutBody: A Peruvian platform that manages alternate bearing in olive groves. We measure winter chill, fruit load and thinning with field nodes and offline sampling, so every season depends on data, not on each year's luck.

features.line1: Viora reads the load of your grove,
features.line2: tracks the chill of every winter
features.line3: and tells you when to thin.
features.line4: Steadier harvests.

modules.lead: This is how Viora supports every stage of your season, from winter to harvest.
modules.loadBody: Sample your trees, even without signal, and know the real load of every lot before the season decides for you.
modules.chillBody: Viora adds up each winter's chill portions for your variety, table or oil, and warns you when a warm winter puts your bloom at risk.
modules.thinningBody: Know how much to thin and until when, for more even calibres and a next season that doesn’t collapse.

off.label: Off year
off.quote: “I don’t know how much I’ll harvest until it’s too late.”
off.pain: A loaded year, then an empty one. The season is planned blind.
off.title: Viora gives you the number before harvest.
off.body: Sample a few trees from your phone, even without signal, and the app works out the target load of the lot and the yield you can expect this season.

chill.label: Low chill
chill.pain: Without enough chill, bloom comes uneven and the fruit set falls short.
chill.title: Viora counts every hour of cold.
chill.body: Weather data adds up the chill portions for your variety, table or oil, and warns you when a warm winter or an El Niño year puts your bloom at risk.

late.label: Late thinning
late.quote: “By the time I wanted to thin, it was already late.”
late.pain: Too much fruit on the tree: small calibres now, a collapse next season.
late.title: Viora opens your thinning window.
late.body: It tells you how much fruit to remove and by when, tree by tree, so calibres even out and next year’s crop holds.

intake.label: Uncertain intake
intake.quote: “I don’t know how much we’ll collect this year.”
intake.pain: Contracts, crews and storage are all set on guesswork.
intake.title: Viora projects your whole intake.
intake.body: It rolls every member’s estimate into one projection, so contracts, crews and storage are planned before the harvest starts.

tacna.statement: Tacna grows 81% of Peru's olives, yet every season is decided blind: one year there's fruit to spare, the next there's not enough.
tacna.copy: In 2024, growers in La Yarada reported losses of up to 90%. In September 2025, a record rebound. They aren't two different stories: they're the two faces of the same ON/OFF cycle.
tacna.statOffLabel: seasons end in an OFF year
tacna.pictureAlt: A young grower looks up, dreaming of a branch heavy with olives
tacna.placeTitle: Between La Yarada and Los Palos
tacna.placeCopy: Sand, sun and wells: this is where most of the country's olives are grown. Viora orders this grove's season — it measures the load, tracks the chill and sets the thinning window — so next year stops depending on chance.
